title: DPD 2.5-degree clusters per spot rose across 1981 after spatial-mixture controls
abstract: We test whether latitude, hemisphere and station mix explain changes in Debrecen groups and position clusters per spot across January 1981. We compare November 1978-December 1980 with January 1981-June 1983. A fractional mass method preserves exact group and cluster counts across spatial cells. At a common 5-degree latitude mix, fine 2.5-degree clusters per spot rise by 15.27% (conditional 95% six-month block interval 4.84% to 29.78%). The group factor is 0.976 (0.893-1.108) and the 6-degree cluster factor is 1.002 (0.909-1.133). Gyula-only, central-disk and all-umbra checks retain the fine-cluster rise. In Gyula alone, shared support exceeds 99.8% on each side and latitude mix contributes -0.00546 groups per spot (-0.00960 to -0.00253) to the raw difference. These descriptive results show that spatial mix is a material control. They do not identify a grouping-rule change, a solar cause or an emission change. One cycle window, preliminary source files and conditional pointwise intervals limit inference. Code, aggregate estimates, hashes and external retrieval instructions are supplied. External observations and derived record tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Post/pre groups and position clusters per spot at a common station, hemisphere and latitude mix, and an exact decomposition of period-rate changes. Intervals use six-month calendar blocks. The tests do not establish a solar cause.
